claims.text: The proposed approach combines high-fidelity DFT, on-the-fly machine learning, and an analytical treatment of atomic-mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Atomic-mass and force-constant disorder mediates phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Atomic-mass and force-constant disorder is equivalent to chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicitly modeling force-constant fluctuations will make lattice thermal-conductivity predictions more accurate.
Separately modeling phonon scattering and electronic transport will produce distinct temperature-dependent lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity trends.
The proposed method will improve prediction accuracy by approximately 20–30% relative to earlier Debye-temperature and averaged-elastic-property models.
The method will resolve lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions separately below 200 K.
Lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below 200 K.
Predicted lattice thermal conductivity will agree with experiment within a 20–30% margin of error over 300–1200 K.
Earlier approaches conflate lattice and electronic contributions and therefore cannot capture their separation below 200 K.
The relevant baseline approaches rely on Debye-temperature estimates and DFT-derived averaged elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity approximations.
The method's most robust applicability is to nearly ideal, defect-free, minimally oxygen-contaminated HfNbTaTiZr between 300 and 1200 K.
The method's validity may diminish when HfNbTaTiZr contains significant extrinsic defects or impurities.
Predictions below 200 K will have increased uncertainty because lattice and electronic transport are closely coupled there.
Keeping oxygen below 1 wt.% isolates intrinsic atomic-scale disorder from extrinsic-defect effects.
Terahertz spectroscopy can independently determine the electronic thermal-transport component needed for deconvolution.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% accuracy improvement over baseline models across 300–1200 K will falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to resolve distinct lattice and electronic contributions below 200 K will falsify the hypothesis.
